title: Unified Inference — Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap & Pricing (Q1 2027)
author: Lena Chen
content:
Overview
--------
This document consolidates the product overview, PRD (requirements), high-level design notes, roadmap & themes, pricing/packaging guidance, and release notes for the Unified Inference product as of Q1 2027. It is intended for product, engineering, go-to-market, solutions, and support teams to align on scope, milestones, and commercial positioning.

Product overview
----------------
Unified Inference is Redwood Inference’s unified runtime and control plane that provides a single developer experience for running model inference across Hosted API, Dedicated (reserved capacity), and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. The product goal is to make production LLM inference predictable in latency, cost, and reliability while enabling customers to choose the deployment mode that meets their security and economics.

Key problems we solve
- Variable latency and throughput across model families and cloud regions that break SLAs.
- High and unpredictable unit token costs for production workloads.
- Fragmented operational tooling between hosted and private deployments.
- Risk of quality regressions during model rollouts.

Primary user personas
- Product/ML Engineers building LLM-powered features (chat, summarization, retrieval-augmented generation).
- Platform teams standardizing inference across business units.
- Security/compliance teams evaluating private deployments and auditability.

Goals & success metrics (12 months)
- 99.9% platform availability for Hosted API endpoints (SLO).
- p95 generation latency <= 650ms for 512-token typical requests on S1 models.
- Reduce per-token cost by 20% across typical enterprise workloads via batching + caching recommendations.
- Achieve NPS >= 30 in PLG onboarding flows for inference customers.

Product requirements (PRD) — prioritized
Must-have (MVP):
1. Single REST/SDK interface for text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking (backwards-compatible with current Redwood API).
2. Model catalog with curated and verified performance profiles (latency, throughput, memory).
3. Basic rollout controls: model pinning, canary traffic (10%), and automated fallback to lower-cap variants.
4. Batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization profile selection exposed as runtime hints.
5. Per-route observability: tokens, latency, error rates, and cost breakdown that map to customer billing.
6. SLA & authentication model for Dedicated and Private (API key, mTLS, RBAC integration).

Should-have (post-MVP quarter 1-2):
- Automated optimization suggestions (batch size, cache TTL, quantization) with expected cost/latency delta.
- Canary + A/B rollout UI in Redwood Console and API hooks for rollback.
- Fine-grained audit logs and KMS/HSM integration for Private deployments.

Nice-to-have (year 2):
- Multi-tenant pooling for Dedicated customers with predictable isolation.
- Adaptive routing between models/regions based on latency and unit economics.

Requirements table (MVP)
| Requirement | Owner | Success Criteria | Priority | Target Release |
|-------------|-------|------------------|----------|----------------|
| REST/SDK parity | SDK & API | SDK passes compatibility test-suite | Must | MVP |
| Model catalog | Applied ML | 10 open models profiled with latency/throughput | Must | MVP |
| Rollouts (canary/fallback) | Runtime | Canary traffic configurable + auto rollback on error spike | Must | MVP |
| Batching & caching API | Serving runtime | 20% cost savings on synthetic RPS tests | Must | MVP |

Design notes & constraints
- Serving runtime: reuse Kernel and scheduling work from eng-serving-runtime. Runtime will expose a policy layer that maps incoming requests to model variants, batches, and caches.
- Compatibility: maintain the current Redwood API shape for text generation; add optional fields for runtime_hints, routing_policy, and quant_profile.
- Security: Private deployments must support customer-managed KMS and provide audit logs in the prescribed format (JSON lines with request_id, user_id, model_id, tokens_in/out).
- Observability: instrument token-level tracing and costs. Console dashboards must link request traces to billing keys.

High-level architecture (summary)
- API gateway -> Routing policy engine -> Model serving pool(s) -> Cost & observability sink.
- Components: Control plane (config, rollouts, catalog), Data plane (runtime kernels, caches), Telemetry pipeline (metrics, traces, billing).

Design spec excerpt: request routing policy schema (example)
- routing_policy: [string enum: latency_preferred | cost_preferred | region_preferred]
- fallback_order: [list of compatible model IDs, e.g. redwood-rlhf-13b-q8 -> redwood-13b-q4]
- cache_ttl_ms: integer

Example CLI for canary rollout
1. Create canary config: redwood rollout create --name website-chat-canary --model redwood-13b-q4 --percent 10 --policy latency_preferred
2. Monitor: redwood rollout status website-chat-canary --watch
3. Promote: redwood rollout promote website-chat-canary --to 100

Roadmap & themes (next 6 quarters)
Q1 2027 (Current): MVP launch for Unified Inference Hosted + Dedicated baseline
- Deliver model catalog + runtime hints API.
- Release Redwood Console rollout controls (API + basic UI).
- GA pricing for Hosted API tokens and Dedicated reserved capacity baseline.

Q2 2027: Optimization tooling
- Redwood Optimize suggestions integrated into Console.
- Automated batching policies and adaptive cache TTL tuning.

Q3 2027: Private & compliance hardening
- Customer HSM/KMS integrations, extended audit logs, SOC2 evidence updates.
- On-prem packaging improvements and day-2 ops documentation.

Q4 2027: Advanced routing and cost-aware fallbacks
- Multi-region routing, dynamic fallback policies, and per-tenant capacity pooling for Dedicated.

Themes driving roadmap
- Production economics: measurable cost/latency tradeoffs as first-class controls.
- Observability & guardrails: tie quality/regression alerts to evals and prompt sets.
- Enterprise readiness: security, private deployments, and long-term support.

Pricing & packaging notes
- Hosted API (self-serve): usage-based pricing by unit tokens and embeddings. Pricing tiers:
  - Developer: $0.0006 / prompt token, $0.0012 / completion token (trial + low-volume cap).
  - Business: $0.00045 / prompt token, $0.0009 / completion token (includes 30-day retention; usage discounts beyond 1M tokens/mo).
  - Enterprise: custom volume pricing + premium SLAs.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly committed GPU pools. Pricing model: base platform fee + per-GPU equivalent price; discounts at 6/12-month commitments.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): license + deployment support fee + optional managed upgrades. KMS/HSM, audit retention, and professional services billed separately.

Packaging guidance for GTM
- Self-serve onboarding for Developer & Business tiers with prebuilt templates (chat, summarization, RAG).
- Sales-assisted Dedicated for >$10k/month committed usage or security requirements.
- Enterprise motion for Private deployments—close with a solutions engineer-led onboarding and a 90-day success plan.

Release notes — Unified Inference v1.0 (2027-02-10)
Summary
- Public launch of Unified Inference Hosted API with model catalog (initial 12 models profiled).
- Console rollout controls (canary, pin, promote) and basic per-route observability released.
- GA pricing for Hosted API and published Dedicated baseline pricing.
Highlights
- Model catalog: each model entry includes p50/p95 latency (512 tokens), max batch throughput, and memory footprint.
- Runtime: batching and KV-prefix caching enabled by default for eligible routes; customers can override via runtime_hints.
- Rollouts: API + Console support for canary (percent), promote, and auto-rollback on error rate > 2x baseline.
Known issues & mitigations
- Large-context workloads (>2048 tokens) can trigger high p95 latencies in some model families. Mitigation: recommend segmented streaming and raise fetch concurrency limits for Dedicated.
- Initial cost-estimator may underpredict for high-variance workload patterns. Mitigation: include conservative buffers and promote Redwood Optimize recommendations.
Operational runbook (on-call summary)
1. If Hosted API p95 latency > 1s for >10 minutes: escalate to eng-platform and eng-serving-runtime on-call.
2. If error rate spike > 1% sustained for 5 minutes: trigger automatic rollback for active canaries; assess root cause.
3. Dedicated capacity underprovisioning: notify SRE & sales ops; offer temporary burst tokens to affected customers.

Ownership & next steps

- PM success criteria for Q1: launch self-serve onboarding, achieve <1 week mean time to first successful request for Business tier, and complete initial sales enablement materials.
